view: iMDx is pre-revenue (Q2 revenue $239K) and its value rests on De Novo authorization of the GraftAssureDx kit. The kit was submitted on 2026-03-25; FDA asked for more information in late July, and the company held an SIR meeting before responding. On my own arithmetic ($18.7M less one quarter at the guided $8M), cash at Sep 30 is about $10.7M, leaving roughly one quarter of runway at that burn. The Q2 10-Q concluded there was no substantial doubt about going concern for 12 months, relying on management's plans. A 10-Q filed in mid-November with about $10M of cash can hardly repeat that unless money has been raised. So the release or 10-Q is likely to show either going-concern language or a financing, with the cleansing release making an overnight deal possible. FDA timing has already been edged toward 2027 by management's own October wording, and the stock is down about 52% since late September. The market is therefore visibly pricing slippage and dilution, though I cannot show how much. Against that, the stock has sold off into the print on low volume at its 52-week low, which also happened before the May print (+25.9%). Any upbeat FDA wording (response filed, interactive review, decision near) or a burn below $8M could bounce it. Bad outcomes (an offering at a discount, -15 to -25%) are larger than good ones, but the steady drawdown makes a modest relief move about as likely as a modest drop when no deal comes. I lean slightly down and see no clean unpriced edge.

recommendation.reason: The decisive facts (about one quarter of cash, likely going-concern language or an imminent raise, FDA slipping toward 2027) are public, and a 52% drawdown in eight weeks shows the market is already pricing them. I cannot show it has priced them too little rather than too much. The lean is down only because an overnight offering would hit the open hard, and I put that at roughly a one-in-four chance.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Down is my lean. It flips up if the release reports FDA authorization or a clearly imminent decision (response filed, interactive review closing), or cash sustained without an offering (Bio-Rad or another non-dilutive deal).

self_critique: The case for a stronger down call: about one quarter of cash, a likely going-concern headline and a cleansing release make an overnight discounted offering quite plausible, and a Lucid initiation in August fits a banker lining up. That leg could take 20% or more off the open. The case for up: after a 52% slide on thin volume with tax-loss season under way, a release saying the FDA response is in and authorization is near could produce a squeeze like May's +25.9%. The two roughly offset, which is why I stay near 50 and make no call.
